comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 1. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 1 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 0; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 0. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '07'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn/reveal a life through $436A, then repeatedly check bomb collection through $436D. Zero remaining count at $3013 exits through success vector $3030 after setting divisor 9; death state $4028=2 waits for state 0, then respawns unless lives sentinel $40E4=$FF, which exits through $3032. Both exits call the header cleanup pointer. This variant also silences SID voice 3 when death state 2 is reached.

Patch local JSR operand from little-endian header $301D/$301E, invoke cleanup, return. In this file the header resolves to shared no-op RTS at $301F; the assembled $FFFF target is a placeholder, not a real call.

Fourth callback requests playerdeath only on nonzero $402B, collisionmasknonzero, and no projectile bits 1..3 in mask $4088. Then always jumps to enemy-hit processing $3373. Projectile collisions therefore change which global mask combinations kill the player.

Drawing data $30B5-$30E2 read by Initial scenery $30B5. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

1 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.
Expand all eight 30-byte compact frames at $31D1 into sprite workspace $8400-$85FF. Remaining state begins zero in overlay file.

Third callback skips zero $402C and deathstate 2, processes sprites 7 down 4. Inactive target state resets velocities, chooses random 9-bit X, starts Y38, colour 7, pointer 10 and enabled 16, then becomes state 1.

State 1 targets have a 1-in 64 chance each update to choose among four velocity tuples: down 2, right 4, down 2, left 4. Cycle frames 10..13, move X with 9-bit wrap, add Y and remove onceY>=220. State>=2 branches to falling animation $330F.
Four eight-byte indexed arrays addressed by sprite index 4..7: state 0 inactive/1 flying/2 shot, dx-low, dx-high, dy. Elements 0..3 of each array are reserved by the sprite-indexed layout.
Eight compact 30-byte frames expanded by $4376. First four animate normal flying targets; last four are their tumbling/shot variants. Player projectiles use resident sprite pointer 38 instead.
Saved target index across RNG calls, followed by firing cooldown. A launched shot sets cooldown 8; first IRQ callback decrements it and forces fire released while nonzero.
Three four-byte arrays: dx-low 0,4,0,FC; dx-high 0,0,0,FF; dy 2,0,2,0. The four two-bit choices include down twice and each horizontal direction once.
Four four-byte arrays indexed 1..3: active flags, X delta low, X delta high, Y delta. Element 0 reserved. Up to three simultaneous projectiles map directly to sprites 1..3.
Sixteen joystick-low-nibble indexed X delta low bytes. Active-low right/diagonals produce+6; left/diagonals produceFA(-6); neutral/vertical produce 0.
Sixteen signed Y deltas: active-low down gives+3, up givesFD(-3), horizontal/neutral 0, with appropriate diagonals.
Sixteen high bytes for X delta table $32DF:FF for left-moving entries,00 otherwise.

State 2 targets fall 3 pixels per update, animate frames 14..17 and cycle colour while $334A produces a descending SID slide. AtY>=220 clear state/enable/coordinates and silence voice 3; then continue remaining targets.
Directly drive SIDvoice 3 pulse frequency derived from negative targetY, pulsewidth 6666, attack 0/sustain 40 and control 41; called for each falling shot target.

Search flying targets7 down4. A nonplayer collision mask containing a projectile bit marks one falling and adds25 to the24-bit score, leaving bonus unchanged. These are whole VIC masks, not pair identities. Native joystick replay UP+RIGHT+FIRE confirms a wrong-target hit: shot3 overlaps alien4 while aliens5/6 overlap separately, so shared mask$78 selects alien6. At$3394 X=6; after$33AF its state changes1 to2 and score0 to25 while player stays alive. Actual sprite registers, original opaque-pixel pairs and state reads agree; see reference/shooting-live-verification.json. CPU checks also cover score carry, falling/removal/respawn and controlled masks.

Consume fire even for neutral direction, full slots or cooldown. Launch into first free shot1..3 and set cooldown8: next eight callback calls are blocked, next possible launch is call9. CPU checked all eight joystick directions, slot/boundary cases; native DOWN+FIRE launches slot1 at32,56. Direction selects velocity tables; sprite pointer$38, noise stream$342C at priority3/release0/noise$80. Native UP+RIGHT+FIRE for240 frames after normal spawn produces three25-point hits and ends with the player dying. The first selects a distant alien because separate contacts share the same collision mask; ordinary controls only after selected-level initialization. A no-fire control scores0 and leaves all four targets flying.
Seven-byte noise sound stream: envelope 19/00, frequency 2020 held 24 ticks, stop 0; selected for each launched projectile.

Second IRQ callback runs on nonzero $402C and outside deathstate 2. Add signed 16-bit X and 8-bit Y deltas for slots 1..3. Remove if half-X<6 or>=172, or Y<6 or>=220, clearing activeflag, Xlow, enable and frame pointer.
Unused loaded 00/FF memory-fill pattern after the projectile loop; identical byte-for-byte to PLF03 at the same addresses. No reachable script/table points into this tail.
